prompt: Match each part of OpenTelemetry to what it does.

pairs.right: What application code calls to start a span
Samples, batches and hands spans on
Agreed attribute names such as db.system

prompt: What does Azure Monitor's OpenTelemetry distro add to the plain OpenTelemetry SDK?

choices.text: Its own span format, which replaces OpenTelemetry's spans entirely
choices.why: It keeps OpenTelemetry's spans and maps them at export.

choices.text: The Azure exporter and automatic instrumentation, wired together
choices.why: Right. One call configures what you would otherwise assemble.

choices.text: A requirement to run the old Application Insights SDK alongside it
choices.why: It replaces that SDK for new work.

choices.text: Live metrics without a connection string
choices.why: Every route to Application Insights needs the connection string.

prompt: Why do the CLIENT spans print before the SERVER span in the transcript?

choices.text: The console exporter sorts spans by kind
choices.why: It sorts nothing; it prints as spans end.

choices.text: The CLIENT calls started first
choices.why: The SERVER span started first and contains them.

choices.text: Each is printed as it ends
choices.why: Right. The parent ends after its last child.

choices.text: SimpleSpanProcessor delays the parent on purpose
choices.why: It exports each span immediately on its end.

prompt: The slow checkout's trace has no `POST /v1/charges` span. Which part of the program explains it?

choices.text: insert_order raised, so checkout never called charge
choices.why: Right. The except clause caught it after the insert, skipping the payment.

choices.text: The sampler dropped the payment span
choices.why: No sampler is configured; every span is kept.

choices.text: CLIENT spans that end in ERROR are left out of the export
choices.why: INSERT orders was exported with ERROR.

choices.text: charge runs in another thread and was lost
choices.why: Everything runs in one thread here.

prompt: Why does a real service use BatchSpanProcessor rather than SimpleSpanProcessor?

choices.text: Batching also samples the spans it collects
choices.why: Sampling is a separate decision, made before processing.

choices.text: So a slow exporter never slows a request
choices.why: Right. Spans are queued and sent from a background thread.

choices.text: Simple exports only to the console
choices.why: It works with any exporter.

choices.text: Azure Monitor refuses spans sent one at a time
choices.why: The reason is the request path, not the receiver.

prompt: A span that handles an incoming request has the kind ___.
hint: In capitals, as the transcript prints it.

prompt: Match each OpenTelemetry item to where the Azure Monitor exporter puts it.
hint: Kinds become tables; ids become columns.

prompt: A checkout passes through shop-api and then an orders service. What keeps both services' rows under one OperationId?
hint: The trace context has to travel.

choices.text: Both services using the same connection string to send
choices.why: That decides where rows land, not how they join.

choices.text: Both services sharing a cloud role name
choices.why: Role names tell services apart; sharing one would hide which is which.

choices.text: The traceparent header passed on the call between them
choices.why: Right. OpenTelemetry's HTTP instrumentation sends and reads it.

choices.text: A join on TimeGenerated in the workspace, after the fact
choices.why: Time is not an identity, as lesson 11 said.

prompt: To send shop_trace.py's spans to Application Insights, which lines change?
hint: Only one block knows where telemetry goes.

choices.text: Every span's attributes, renamed to Azure's names
choices.why: The attributes are semantic conventions; the exporter maps them.

choices.text: The setup block
choices.why: Right. Everything below it is vendor-neutral.

choices.text: The span kinds, from SERVER to REQUEST
choices.why: There is no REQUEST kind; SERVER maps to AppRequests.

choices.text: None; the console exporter also sends to Azure
choices.why: It prints to the terminal and nowhere else.

prompt: What can a stranger do with the shop's Application Insights connection string?

choices.text: Read every request the shop recorded
choices.why: Reading needs an identity with a role on the workspace.

choices.text: Delete the Application Insights resource
choices.why: Deletion is a Resource Manager operation with its own permissions.

choices.text: Send telemetry to it, and raise the bill
choices.why: Right. It authorises ingestion, not reading.

choices.text: Nothing at all, because it is encrypted
choices.why: It is plain text; what it allows is ingestion.

prompt: A team moves from Azure Monitor to another backend through an OpenTelemetry Collector. What is most of the work?

choices.text: Re-instrumenting every service from the start
choices.why: The spans are vendor-neutral and stay as they are.

choices.text: Changing the exporter in each service
choices.why: With a collector, the services may not change at all.

choices.text: Rewriting queries, alerts and dashboards
choices.why: Right. KQL written against AppRequests means nothing elsewhere.

choices.text: Converting trace ids to the new format
choices.why: Trace ids are OpenTelemetry's and stay valid.

prompt: Put the life of the slow checkout's database span in order.
items: insert_order opens a CLIENT span as its child
The call times out and the span's status becomes ERROR
The CLIENT span ends and is exported
The SERVER span records the exception, ends and is exported
trap: Exporting the SERVER span before its child is the slip: a parent ends after its children.

prompt: Which of these did this lesson run? Choose all that apply.
hint: The SDK and the console, yes; Azure, no.

choices.text: Two traced checkouts printed by the console exporter
choices.why: Yes. shop_trace.py.

choices.text: configure_azure_monitor() with a connection string
choices.why: No. There is no resource to name.

choices.text: Spans arriving in AppRequests in a workspace
choices.why: No. Lesson 11's tables were generated, not exported.

choices.text: A span ending in ERROR with an exception recorded
choices.why: Yes. The slow checkout.
